A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same WATCH/WCTM research despite the changed title and reorganized appendices. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original synthetic experiments, tabular and image evaluations, detection-delay measurements, and appendix ablations.

after.justification: v4 reports original experiments on the same data domains, including revised detection-delay and runtime estimates and retained appendix analyses.

M1.justification: The reported procedures receive limited corrections: Eq. (15) starts the Shiryaev-Roberts sum at the preceding alarm, and Eq. (17) excludes the adaptation-start observation from the fixed calibration pool. Weighted p-values, composite-jumper betting, and X-CTM-triggered adaptation remain the central components; Appendix C mainly derives the existing implementation.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate synthetic shifts, MEPS, Superconductivity, Bike Sharing, MNIST-C, and CIFAR-10-C with the same regression, classification, and shift-detection coverage. The MEPS root-cause experiment promoted to v4 Section 4.4 already appeared in v1 Appendix D.1.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain standard CTMs, CTM-based Shiryaev-Roberts monitoring, PR-ST, PR-CD-online, and PR-CD-50. The estimator and betting-function ablations also retain their comparator membership.

E3.justification: The retained MEPS root-cause experiment in Figure 4 has revised testing settings: the concept-shift changepoint moves from t=100 to t=500, the monitoring horizon extends, and the WCTM alarm threshold increases. These are changes within an existing scenario rather than new task coverage.

E4.justification: The brightness-corruption case study and MEPS root-cause analysis receive revised trajectories in Figures 3 and 4; Figure 9 also replaces the no-corruption prediction-set-size example. The shift-magnitude, density-ratio-estimator, and betting-function ablations in Figures 5–7 are retained.

E5.justification: The principal quantitative comparisons gain standard errors, absent from v1 Table 1. ADD is reported over 200 rather than 100 seeds, while the separately reported runtimes use 20 seeds. Figure 3 changes from one experiment to an average of five, and Figure 4 reports 200 rather than 100 seeds, substantially revising replication and uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: The main tabular ADD and runtime result sets are revised, alongside trajectories in Figures 3, 4, and 9. For weighted Bike Sharing, SR-WCTM versus PR-CD-online ADD changes from 145.09 versus 162.71 to 155.6 versus 154.3, reversing the point-estimate ordering. Changed run counts and some settings limit direct performance interpretation. The image-corruption numbers in v1 Table 2 are retained in v4 Table 3.

T1.justification: New Appendix C derives the practical weights and introduces an augmented null requiring equality between the calibration-score empirical CDF and population CDF, with associated conditional-coverage reasoning in Eqs. (23)–(29). v4 also explicitly requires exact approximations in Theorem 3.1, revises the covariate-shift null in Eq. (13), and changes the induction justification in Appendix B.

C1.justification: Both versions claim monitoring beyond exchangeability, adaptation to benign shifts, rapid harmful-shift detection, and root-cause diagnosis. v4 emphasizes diagnosis in the abstract, but this contribution was already stated in v1's introduction and conclusion.

C2.justification: Unlike v1, v4 Appendix C explicitly acknowledges that reusing fixed calibration data can make successive p-values dependent, preventing direct application of Theorem 3.1 after adaptation begins. It discusses fresh calibration samples or stronger calibration-distribution assumptions and interprets alarms as potentially reflecting inadequate calibration. This materially qualifies the practical guarantees.

D1.justification: v4 documents the practical weight normalization and explicitly distinguishes changepoint timing for ADD and runtime measurements. It updates the repository pointer from wtr to watch and removes the unfinished Algorithm 3. The architecture and training-configuration tables remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Appendix A adds a connection to online compression models, citing Vovk's single-author 2003 paper and his 2023 paper on forgetting in hypothesis testing. Barber and Tibshirani (2025) is now described as concurrent work. The broader research positioning is retained.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, background explanations, and conclusion are edited. Scheduled monitoring receives its own subsection, existing root-cause analysis moves into Section 4.4, and appendix material is reorganized. Much of the original prose and overall narrative remains intact.

P2.justification: The combined ADD/runtime table becomes two separately structured tables with standard errors, while the image-corruption table moves to the appendix. Figure 4 is redrawn and promoted to the main text, Figures 3 and 9 change plot scales or panels, and Figure 8 is consolidated onto one page. These substantially reorganize the presentation of empirical evidence.

improvement.justification: v4 improves transparency by exposing the fixed-calibration validity gap in Appendix C and adding standard errors to the main quantitative comparisons. The gains remain limited: practical guarantees require strong additional assumptions, and some speed statements conflict with the revised evidence—SR-WCTM does not outperform PR-CD-online on Bike Sharing in Table 1, while PR-CD-50 has the lowest runtimes in Table 2.
